issue.body:
Record how search shards handle commit notifications with respect to prefetching, so we can tell how long prefetches take and how often they are skipped. Unlike `es.bcc.notification_time.histogram`, the duration is not capped by the timeout that releases the VBCC on indexing shards.

`SearchCommitPrefetcher#maybePrefetchLatestCommit` now reports a `PrefetchResult` (`disabled`, `idling`, `skipped`, `foreground`, `background`) through its listener. Two metrics are recorded from it:

- `es.stateless.search.commit_prefetch.total`: one sample per notification handled by the prefetcher, tagged with the prefetch `type` and whether the notified BCC was `uploaded`. Notifications for which the prefetch failed, or that were received while the store was closing, are not counted.
- `es.stateless.search.commit_prefetch.duration.histogram`: time in milliseconds from the start of a prefetch until it completes, tagged with the same `type` (only `foreground` or `background`, as skipped notifications have no duration) and `uploaded` attributes. Failed prefetches are recorded too, and cannot be told apart.

Notes:

- `uploaded` reflects the notified commit's BCC, not the BCC that is actually prefetched. When prefetching of non-uploaded commits is disabled, a prefetch with `uploaded=false` targets an older uploaded BCC.
- The metrics are named `commit_prefetch` to avoid confusion with `es.blob_cache.prefetch.total`, which counts the read-path `tryPrefetch` attempts.

Recording is disabled by default and controlled by the dynamic setting `stateless.search.prefetch_commits.metrics.enabled`, so it can be turned on for specific projects only.

issue.title: Allow merged-segment warming to run asynchronously off the merge thread
issue.body:
Today a merged segment warmer (`IndexWriter.IndexReaderWarmer` set using `IndexWriterConfig#setMergedSegmentWarmer`) runs synchronously on the merge thread, right before the writer publishes the new segment. The merge thread stays blocked for the whole duration of warming.

I use a warmer very much like the one in the replicator package (`PreCopyMergedSegmentWarmer`): it opens a reader on the freshly merged segment and does real work on it before that segment becomes visible. In my case warming isn't cheap and while it runs the merge thread is pinned doing no merge related work. So other pending merges queue up behind it even though the heavy `mergeMiddle` work for that merge is already done.

I'd like to propose making warming optionally asynchronous. The merge thread would finish writing the merge, hand the warming off, and immediately be free to pick up the next merge. Warming would happen in the background; the merged segment simply wouldn't be published until the warming completes. The default can stay synchronous so nothing changes unless you opt in.

I think it's worth it: the merge threads are released as soon as the merge is written so warming no longer inteferes with merges throughput. The warming cost (loading structures, pre-copying to replicas, whatever the warmer does) is removed off the critical merge path.

Anecdotally, this would also compound better with something like #16571 (letting a single merge write more than one output segment) since more outputs per merge means more readers to warm per merge, so keeping warming off the merge thread matters even more there.

I gave it a try in #16846 for those who would like to see how it could look. 

The exception handling is the hard part because once warming runs in the background there's no caller left to rethrow to. But it turned out less messy than I expected, mostly because warming happens at the very end after the bulk of the merge work is already done and on disk. I think the publish/commit step can simply run on the warmer thread once warming succeeds. And since a merge that's still warming is kept in the IndexWriter's "running" set the shutdown semantics seem to hold up (ie,  waitForMerges()/close()/rollback() would already block until warming is done).

I see how this change helps avoiding the write amplification due to copying generational files in every first commit of BCCs. The main tradeoff is that projects with fewer updates may create BCCs larger than the 15MB target limit, which seems acceptable to me.

issue.body:
The final assertBusy timed out with commits 18 and 19 still present. They are
created while the target search shard is recovering, and the target
pessimistically registers them. They are released only when the started target
answers a new commit notification, which normally comes from the periodic
inactivity monitor and can exceed 10s under CI load.

Fixed by running the inactivity monitor poll explicitly after closing the PITs and raise
the final assertBusy timeout to 30s.

For FAIL_SOURCE, also wait for the source to free its PIT contexts before 
re-querying the PITs, as already done for SUCCESSFUL_RELOCATION.

Relates #160055

issue.title: Pin every BCC referenced by generational files in mergeMetadata

labels.name: user-26872195/repo-4b2f4cfa
labels.description: Anything around managing Lucene and the Translog in an open shard.

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for distributed team.

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Automatically merge pull request when CI checks pass (NB doesn't wait for reviews!)

issue.body:
When a commit or a relocated PIT context references generational files, SearchDirectory#mergeMetadata only pinned a single BCC term/generation, assuming all generational files in an incoming batch belonged to the same BCC. This holds for new commit notifications, but a relocated PIT carries generational files accumulated across many BCCs over the PIT's lifetime (see mergePITReaderMetadata).

When the PIT commit's own BCC is not yet uploaded, the handoff builds the PIT metadata (OpenPITContextInfo) from the multiple BCCs present in the SearchDirectory of the source search shard. Opening this PIT on the target search shard re-acquires each BCC. If a BCC was not already pinned, the PIT reopening fails with "Cannot acquire [...] for generational file [...]" (swallowed as a WARN), so no relocated context is created and the subsequent PIT search fails with a missing context.

The same single-BCC assumption also breaks on the normal refresh path when a lagging reader advances several commits at once and opens, for the first time, a still-live generational file whose first-seen BCC is older than the one pinned, failing the refresh with the same "Cannot acquire" error.

Impact on the shard differs per path: on PIT relocation the error is swallowed, so the shard stays healthy but the PIT is lost; on the refresh and recovery paths the error propagates and can fail the shard (failed refreshes, dropped commit notifications, and recovery failures).

The fix acquires all distinct BCC term/generations referenced by the incoming generational files and pins them, so opening the PIT or a deferred commit always finds each file's BCC present.

Over the last 90 days this signature accounted for roughly 66k swallowed PIT-relocation WARNs, ~55k dropped commit notifications, and ~400 real shard/recovery failures across the fleet.
